learner_operation: Solve a small consistent dependent linear system using Gauss-Jordan elimination, identify pivot/free variables, and select its full one-parameter vector solution. The learner must establish which whole vector line satisfies the equations, reading pivots and free variables; typography and fixed candidate positions are not part of this operation.

fixed_features.feature: Consistent small systems with one free real parameter
fixed_features.justification: The tutorial and captured solving questions teach full parametric solutions of dependent systems. This isolates the source skill.
All 14 captured practice banks use this response form and conventional original variable ordering.

fixed_features.feature: Later pivot cannot depend on an earlier free variable in RREF
fixed_features.justification: Required by echelon mathematics; canonical pivots x,z and free y therefore make z constant.

answer_roles.role: Which candidate full solution line satisfies the equations
answer_roles.eligible_variation: All five candidate roles can be made correct without changing their mathematical bank.
answer_roles.observed: 30 fixed-bank controls attain all five distinct correct lines across all six cases; native grader and representative renderer agree.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Free z with pivots x,y; canonical free y with pivots x,z; rank-one two-variable form.
answer_roles.observed: All occur in fresh and filtered samples. Canonical original system is explicitly replayed.

answer_roles.role: Constant, vanishing-intercept and equal basic coordinates
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Eligible coordinate assignments and signs can vary while preserving rank and complete solution dimension.
answer_roles.observed: All six visible mathematical cases survive delivery; zero-constant and rational boundaries are retained.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Position should not signal correctness; eligible nonzero slopes/intercepts may be integer or source fractions.
answer_roles.observed: Fresh positions and bank roles vary within templates. Current source banks share supplied nonzero slopes, so unit typography no longer singles out a key. Both unit signs occur in homogeneous controls.

counterfactuals.change: Change one basic-coordinate coefficient while keeping constants, row mixing, seed and free column fixed; separately exchange eligible free-column roles.
counterfactuals.expected: Prompt, keyed full solution and worked explanation follow the new evidence; the former solution is no longer accepted.
counterfactuals.observed: Integer and rational pairs change their answers and explanations; native stale-response cases reject the old vector. Canonical alternate free-column result agrees with the original source.
counterfactuals.justification: Tutorial basic/free-variable reasoning and canonical free-y example require deriving answers from equations, rather than fixed coordinate assignments.

counterfactuals.change: Keep the five candidate lines fixed; force each candidate role in turn and derive corresponding equations.
counterfactuals.expected: All five assignments can be correct under appropriate same-method evidence, with matching explanations and native keys.
counterfactuals.observed: Each of six cases retains its complete unordered bank while all five different lines become correct; 150 actual native choice outcomes match. Representative role pair rendered and visually inspected.
counterfactuals.justification: Which source object satisfies the mathematical rule is incidental. Fixed-bank intervention tests answer roles independently of numeric surface variation.

counterfactuals.change: Change invertible row mixing while preserving the RREF solution line.
counterfactuals.expected: The printed system and row-operation explanation change, while the complete solution remains accepted.
counterfactuals.observed: Both integer and rational pairs preserve the answer and native acceptance of the previous vector; screenshots show changed equations and unchanged solution.
counterfactuals.justification: Elementary row operations preserve the source system solution set, so this is irrelevant to the final response despite changing presentation.
